newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Blacks aquire R400 mln stake in SAfricas Zenex Oil.
newsitem.headline: Blacks aquire R400 mln stake in SAfricas Zenex Oil.

text.p: Worldwide African Investment Holdings (Pty) Ltd said on Sunday it had completed a 400 million rand ($88 million) acquisition of Zenex Oil in the first major breakthrough by black investors into South Africa's oil industry.

The Johannesburg-based investment company -- managed and owned by a black empowerment group of emerging entrepreneurs -- has taken a controlling 51 percent stake in Zenex, a move which complements its launch in 1995 of Afric Oil in a joint venture with Caltex.

The transaction, which was negotiated on behalf of the Zenex Trustees by BOE Natwest, is the biggest deal yet concluded by Worldwide African Investment Holdings (WAIH) and is the first transaction giving black investors effective control of a fully operational oil company, Zenex said in a statement.

Caltex chairman Mike Rademeyer said the deal fulfilled Caltex's original intention of creating the black empowerment oil company Afric Oil which, after having created value through large volume business, would expand and significantly increase its operations in the liquid fuel industry.

"This purchase offers WAIH the opportunity to substantially expand its role in the oil industry through the acquisition of an existing, fully fleged oil company and by merging Afric Oil with Zenex," the statement said.
WAIH heads a consortium also comprising, Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank and Zenex management. WAIH has pre-emptive rights to increase its shareholding.
Zenex has 150 service stations, 20 country depots, a lubricant blending plant in Durban, terminals in Cape Town, Alrode and Durban, and a stake in Durban's marine bunker fuel facilities.
In contrast, Afric Oil is strictly a sales operation, with 52 service stations providing an entry point to the industry for black entrepreneurs.

Zenex's 1996 turnover topped 1.4 billion rand. Its total annual sales volume is in excess of 660 million litres. It does not have a stake in a refinery. With this exception, Zenex is a fully integrated oil company serving agricultural, commercial, retail and marine consumers.
Zenex and Sasol are the only major oil industry players which are fully South African owned.
Zenex was sold by The Zenex 1995 Trust, a Jersey-based trust which acquired the company in the wake of a 1987 disinvestment by a major U.S. oil company.
The deal was completed on the basis of no enforced job losses and management continuity. Zenex has 150 employees.
